$comment: Versions of Soquel that were withdrawn. Read by the running app on launch when Settings > Updates > 'Warn me if this build is known to be faulty' is on, which it is by default. Exact versions only, never ranges.

advisories.summary: Opening the Branches panel and pressing Diff with Current can empty one of your files.
advisories.detail: A branch whose name begins with a dash was passed to git as an option instead of as a branch. Git reads --output=<file> as an instruction to write over that file, so the click emptied it. Any file you can write could be hit, and there is no undo. It needs a repository that carries such a branch, so a repository you cloned rather than one you made. 1.1.1 refuses those names and no longer lets a branch name be read as an option.

advisories.summary: Cancelling an update installs it anyway.
advisories.detail: The Cancel button on the install dialog closed the window but did not stop the download. The application was replaced regardless, and then offered to restart. Also in these versions, Settings > Default App > "Open the folder Finder was going to" asked for permission to control Finder and then did nothing with the answer. Both are fixed in 1.2.2.

advisories.summary: Updating asks for your login password to reach your saved API key.
advisories.detail: The key for Clean This Folder was kept in the Keychain, whose access control trusts the exact binary that wrote the item. Every update is a different binary, so every update challenged it and asked for a login password to reach a key you had already given. 1.5.1 keeps the key in a 0600 file instead and never asks.
